title: Stroke sculpting: strokes as surface curves on the base, one pass, synced across all 8 views
user-messages:
> What we give up with one pass:

if you need two passes I think it would be better to save off the model and write a new dsl, since the chain is too hard to reason about


yes write the ticket
yes stop the agent and have another agent fix mes-86
description:
Stroke sculpting stores each stroke as 2D pixels in one view's SVG and re-casts it, on every evaluation, through that view's camera onto whatever mesh the previous stroke_sculpt node left. A sculpt is a chain of such nodes, so a stroke lands on a surface the earlier nodes have moved. The blind skull run (MESH-79) shows the cost:
- The side-view bite line and the front-view teeth ticks drift apart once `profile` pushes the face forward. The front strokes cast along the push; the side strokes cast across it.
- Editing an early node silently moves every later node's strokes.
- Strokes inside one node all land on the same input and cannot see each other (MESH-81).
- The same feature drawn in two views has no link between its two drawings.
- The chain is too hard to reason about, for the user and for the sculptor.

Make the stroke a surface curve on the base mesh, applied in one pass, with SVG kept as the format the LLM edits.

1. Stored truth: every stroke is a curve on the base mesh (the fixed mesh the sculpt loads, e.g. skull3/base.ply), held as base face plus barycentric per point. Reuse the ring scene's surface-path code (TracedSurfacePath, SurfaceSpline / SurfaceSplineTracer in geometry/mesh/data/paths/) rather than StrokeSketch's loose ray-hit points. Each stroke has a stable id and its settings (data-radius, data-depth, kind, profile, smooth). It lives in a sidecar file beside the SVGs.
2. One pass: every stroke's displacement is computed on the base and summed; the sculpt is the base plus the sum, with one refinement whose new vertices map back to base faces. Named layers stay as organisation only (one SVG or <g id> per part), not as an order of operations. When a sculpt genuinely needs a second pass, the answer is to save the result as a new base mesh and start a new DSL on it, never a chain of stroke_sculpt nodes (the user's rule). The node should refuse a stroke_sculpt input that is itself a stroke_sculpt output.
3. Projection: each stroke is carried to its place on the finished sculpt and drawn into every one of the 8 multiview cells that sees it, with the same id in each. Visible spans are solid; hidden spans are dashed and marked data-hidden, so the line is continuous. The SVGs are overwritten from the stored curves.
4. Editing stays plain SVG: move a point, add a polyline, delete one, in any cell. A sync command (ixdar-cli sculpt-sync) diffs each SVG against the version it last wrote:
   - A moved point is cast through that cell's camera onto the finished sculpt and mapped back to its base face.
   - A polyline with no id is a new stroke.
   - A missing id deletes its stroke.
   - The same stroke edited in two views since the last sync is refused, naming both.
   Then it rewrites all 8 views. Points carry their curve index (data-pts) so a moved SVG vertex maps to its stored point; a missing or duplicate id gets a refusal with a fix.

Trade-offs to handle, not dodge:
- Displacement runs along the base's normals, not the already-sculpted surface's.
- Overlapping strokes add, so MESH-81's interference must be fixed in the summation, not avoided by ordering.

Split if too large into (a) stroke ids, the base-anchored sidecar and the one-pass sum; (b) 8-view projection and sculpt-sync; (c) migrating skull3 and the stroke_sculpt samples.

Bugs found by the run-4 sculptor (MESH-88, round 1; its notes are /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/.claude/worktrees/mesh-88/tmp/frictions.md, comparison pictures tmp/cmp_front.png synced vs tmp/exp/nosync_cmp.png unsynced, sculpt dsl/skull4/skull.{dsl,svg,strokes} in that worktree). The run is stopped until these are fixed:
1. sculpt-sync lifts new strokes onto whatever mesh the viewer shows (the last sculpt, with its holes), not the base: redrawn strokes land 10-20 px from where they were drawn. Sync must always lift onto the node's base input, whatever is loaded.
2. A bowl fill held in the .strokes sidecar cuts through the side wall of the head (eye socket opens out to the Front silhouette, flaps in the 3/4 views), while the same SVG lifted through its camera with no sidecar gives a clean socket. Find why the anchored fill differs from the camera-lifted one (fill region, depth direction, visibility) and make them match.
3. With the source .strokes file deleted, stroke_sculpt silently reads a stale copy from ixdar-app/target/classes/. The sidecar must be read beside the SVG that was actually resolved, never from a build copy.
4. Regenerating the SVG without data-ids renumbers every stroke on each sync (s1.., s95..); give strokes stable ids (e.g. from the group id and order) so a regenerated drawing keeps them.
5. stroke-report names strokes "shape N" without a sidecar and "stroke sN" with one; use one naming.
6. multiview --camera with a path that runs through a file and `..` returns a bare HTTP 500; return a message naming the path.
7. stroke-report reports "moved N vertices" both for a ridge whose sparse points move the surface only in dashes and for a bowl fill of radius 0.04 that terraces into ripples; flag both (point spacing too wide for the radius; radius too small for the mesh's edge length), and say the rule in the stroke_sculpt catalog entry.
definition-of-done:
Strokes are stored as base-anchored surface curves with stable ids; one stroke_sculpt pass sums all strokes on the base and refuses a stroke_sculpt input; ixdar-cli sculpt-sync rewrites all 8 views from the curves and folds SVG edits (move, add, delete) back, refusing conflicting or id-less edits with a fix; the same stroke shows with the same id in every view that sees it, hidden spans dashed; tests cover a move in one view appearing in another, add, delete, conflict, and a stroke staying on its feature when another stroke changes; skull3 and the stroke_sculpt samples migrated and loading; StrokeSculpt.apply no longer a single 800-line method.

Split: skull3's migration (MESH-79 not on master) and MESH-81's retest on it moved to MESH-87; the stroke_sculpt samples on master are migrated here.

Each of the seven run-4 bugs fixed or explained, with a StrokeSculptTest/SculptSyncTest case for 1-4; the run-4 round-1 sculpt synced on its base gives eye sockets with intact side walls (before/after captures under tmp/).
testing-plan: Unit tests in StrokeSculptTest for: a point moved in the Front cell's SVG appears moved in the Right cell after sync; add, delete and two-view conflict; a stroke keeps its base face when another stroke is edited. Capture skull3 before/after migration with the strokes overlaid on all 8 cells (teeth ticks and bite line lining up). Load-time and vertex-count before/after in measurements.
unknowns: How MESH-85 (redesign StrokeSculpt.apply) relates: likely superseded by this; decide and close or fold it in.
Whether summed displacement along base normals is close enough on large moves (profile, face_turn), or those belong in a re-based second DSL.
changes-made: (a) One pass, apply redesigned (supersedes MESH-85): StrokeSculpt.apply was one ~810-line method (7,973 bytecode bytes); it is now a 90-line orchestrator (1,006 bytes) over named concepts: SculptStroke with ChainStroke, FillStroke and SilhouetteStroke (parse, reflect, mirror absorb, refine targets, seeds, kernel, deposit), StrokeRefinement (rounds, mirror twins) over MidpointSplit (split closure, Phong-lifted midpoints, crease carry), and DisplacementSum (per-vertex sum, visibility and shadow feather, drag blur, relax). Every StrokeSculptTest passed unchanged through the refactor.

Summation: distinct strokes now add; the copies of one stroke (its reflections) keep the larger move so a stroke meeting its mirror copy leaves no seam; drags and smoothing take the largest. Interference found: the refinement gap rule refined a stroke to a third of its gap to any other stroke, which existed because same-sign strokes took the max (a kink between them). Summed same-sign bumps closer than their radius merge smoothly, so only an opposite-sign neighbour sets a gap now; without that fix stroke_sculpt_sphere's merged rounds refined to 244,850 vertices (round 3 redraws round 1's nose), with it 62,538. MESH-81 itself (far-side pits) still needs MESH-79's layers: MESH-87.

Stored truth: StrokeAnchors, a sidecar <name>.strokes beside the SVG, holds every stroke under a stable id (s1, s2, ...) with its layer (<g id>), home cell, settings and its curve on the base as base face, fan triangle and barycentric u v per point (FaceAnchors: nearest point of the faces around the nearest vertex); silhouettes keep their home-cell pixels, since they are view rays. AnchoredStroke.curve gives the curve as a TracedSurfacePath (every point in-face). The spline tracer was not used for the curve: it snaps anchors to vertices, which would lose a moved point's place inside a face. stroke_sculpt evaluates the sidecar (chains take their base points as they are, fills re-scan their outline in the home cell, onto the base), refuses a sidecar made on another base (vertex and face counts), refuses an SVG with data-id shapes and no sidecar, and says in its report when the SVG was edited since the last sync. The output carries slot _stroke_sculpt (the StrokeSculpt, with the refined unmoved surface), and a stroke_sculpt whose input carries it refuses with the fix (save as a new base, new DSL). Report lines name strokes by id.

(b) Projection and sync: SculptSync.draw carries each base point onto the sculpt (located on the refined unmoved surface, same face and weights on the moved one) and draws it into every cell that sees some of it, under data-id, data-cell and data-pts; spans behind the sculpt are dashed and data-hidden, a wholly visible fill is a polygon, silhouettes only in their own cell, layers as <g id>. SculptSync.fold diffs the SVG against the copy the sidecar keeps of what was last written: moved points are cast through their cell onto the sculpt and held on the base again, a shape with no data-id is added (lifted with the node's own validation), an id gone from a cell deletes the stroke; refused, with the fix and nothing written: a stroke edited in two cells (a delete and a move count as two), an unknown id, a copied span, data-pts not matching the points, a point off the sculpt. StrokeAnchors.sync runs fold, re-evaluates, draws and writes both files; the route mesh/sculpt-sync (generated CLI: ixdar-cli sculpt-sync --dsl [--layer]) runs it per stroke_sculpt node of a DSL, all geometry in Java. A moved point is redrawn where the stroke's own displacement carries it along the base normal, a little past the drag (front cell: 60 px drag drawn 89 px on the cheek ridge).

(c) Samples: stroke_sculpt_head's three chained passes are one pass, head.svg with <g id> outline, face, teeth, synced to head.strokes (8 strokes); pass1-3.svg removed. stroke_sculpt_sphere and stroke_crease_sphere join their three rounds' strokes in one node. Captures tmp/captures/before (MESH-80 tip) vs after: head RMSE 0.61, 35,936 to 31,256 vertices, 0.40 s to 0.25 s; crease identical; sphere RMSE 10.1, same features with the eye sockets and nose summed rather than layered, 49,114 to 62,538 vertices. Numbers in tmp/mesh-86-measurements.json. skull3 is not on master (MESH-79 open): split to MESH-87 with MESH-81's retest. The live stroke-sculpt tool keeps one open pass and refuses a second with the fix. MESH-78's MeshSmoothing.unfold is not on master; its call belongs on the summed pass's final step in StrokeSculpt.apply (marked there) and on MidpointSplit's Phong lift, not duplicated here.

Tests: SculptSyncTest (first sync holds strokes on the base and draws them in every cell that sees them, hidden span dashed in Right; a point moved in Front moves in Right; add and delete; two-cell conflict refused naming both and writing nothing; copied, unknown and miscounted ids refused with the fix; a stroke keeps its base faces when another is edited; a stroke_sculpt output refused as input), StrokeSculptTest 15/15 (the chained-pass test became onePassReplaysExactlyAndKeepsItsCheekWhenTheOutlineIsEdited), full suite 751/751.

Run-4 bugs (MESH-88 round 1). 1 and 2, one cause: SculptSync.fold cast a shape with no data-id onto the layer's last sculpt and carried the hit to the base through the refined surface, so a shape drawn over an earlier pit landed on its floor or through it (the eye-socket outline 10-20 px off, the bowl re-scanned from that outline cutting the head's side wall; 98 fill samples instead of 160). It happened on every sync after the first once the drawing was regenerated without ids. New shapes are now lifted onto the base exactly as stroke_sculpt lifts an SVG with no sidecar (StrokeSketch.lift on the base, the polygon outline cast through a TriangleBvh over the base); moved points are still cast onto the sculpt they are drawn on. Reproduced on a copy of skull4 in tmp/skull4: a regenerated id-less SVG synced over the sidecar now reports the same strokes and 92,019 vertices as the camera lift, and its multiview matches the unsynced one (RMSE 0.0002); before/after in tmp/mesh-86-skull4-synced-{before,after}.png (Front and 3/4, socket walls intact). The viewer's mesh never entered: the route runs its own graph. 3: StrokeAnchors.beside resolved the sidecar path on its own and fell back to the classpath (target/classes); it now reads only beside the SVG file MeshLoader.resolve found, and the classpath only when the SVG itself came from there. 4: a shape with no data-id takes a stable id from its <g id> and its place among that group's id-less shapes (eyes.1, eyes.2; s1.. outside a group), passing over ids still drawn, so a regenerated drawing keeps its ids and the sync reports it redrawn (SculptSync.stableIds). 5: stroke_sculpt's report always says stroke <id>; with no sidecar the id is the one sync will give. 6: left to mesh-80 (coordinator's fix). 7: the dashes were refinement measuring a chain's reach to its points instead of its segments (SculptStroke.requireEdgeLengths now uses elementFraction over a chain's segments, as its kernel does), so a sparse chain now refines and moves like a dense one (5,531 vs 5,575 vertices moved); terracing is a stroke steeper than the finest edges refinement reaches (0.005, or mean edge / 16): the report marks |data-depth| > data-radius^2 / (2.31 x finest edge) TOO STEEP with the limit, and the catalog entry states the rule. Samples: head 31,256 to 31,480 vertices (chains refine between points), sphere and crease unchanged. Tests: SculptSyncTest +3 (a shape added over an earlier pit held where it lands on the base; a drawing regenerated without ids keeps its ids and sculpts as the camera lift does, report naming included; a sidecar read only beside its SVG, not from a build copy on the classpath), both failing with the old lifting; SculptSyncTest 10/10, StrokeSculptTest 15/15, full suite 756/756.
review-summary: stroke_sculpt is now one pass: every stroke is a curve held on the base mesh under a stable id and summed, and ixdar-cli sculpt-sync redraws them in all eight cells and folds plain-SVG edits back. Chained passes made strokes drift and the sculpt impossible to reason about.
